questions_and_answers.question_text: What two forms may be used when addressing someone directly?

answers.answer_text: Either the name plus the title, or the title alone.

questions_and_answers.question_text: How must Xiānsheng be translated when it is used alone, and why?
Why would "Mr." be an inadequate translation of Xiānsheng used on its own?

answers.answer_text: Because "Mr." would not capture the respectful tone that Xiānsheng carries.

questions_and_answers.question_text: What is said about the respectfulness of Tàitai when it is used alone?
How should you address Mrs. Mǎ, according to the note?

answers.answer_text: You should address her as Mǎ Tàitai.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese sentence that means "Mr. Wáng, who is she?"
What is the Chinese sentence meaning "She is Mrs. Mǎ Mínglǐ."?
In exchange 10, the speaker addresses someone using a title alone. Which title is used, and how is it translated?
Which title in these exchanges is used for a married woman, and what is its English equivalent?
Rewrite the direct address in exchange 9 using the title alone instead of the name plus title.

articles.text:
9.  A: Wáng Xiānsheng, tā shi shéi?         Mr. Wáng, who is he?
    B: Tā shi Mǎ Mínglǐ Xiānsheng.         He is Mr. Mǎ Mínglǐ.

10. A: Xiānsheng, tā shi shéi?              Sir, who is he?
    B: Tā shi Mǎ Xiānsheng.                He is Mr. Mǎ.

11. A: Xiānsheng, tā shi shéi?              Sir, who is she?
    B: Tā shi Mǎ Tàitai.                   She is Mrs. Mǎ.

12. A: Wáng Xiānsheng, tā shi shéi?         Mr. Wáng, who is she?
    B: Tā shi Mǎ Mínglǐ Tàitai.            She is Mrs. Mǎ Mínglǐ.

Note on Nos. 9-12

When you address someone directly, use either the name plus the title or the title alone. Xiānsheng must be translated as "sir" when it is used alone, since "Mr." would not capture its respectful tone. (Tàitai, however, is less respectful when used alone. You should address Mrs. Mǎ as Mǎ Tàitai.)
